title: Finite generic fibers become a finite morphism near the generic points
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Y$ be Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact). Suppose the set-theoretic fiber $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ is finite for every generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point] of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y$. Then there exists a dense open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ containing all these generic points such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02NW, label lemma-generically-finite, equivalence (1) and (4), at the finitely many generic points

proof.text: Fix a component generic point η and choose an affine open V₀ containing it. Restrict f to V₀; quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and local finite type are preserved by this restriction. The finite fibre is preserved under the subtype inclusion. Genericity in V₀ follows because every generalization maps to a generalization of η in Y, hence equals η, and the open inclusion is injective. For the restricted map with affine target, Mathlib quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated supplies quasi-separatedness of the source directly; no explicit diagonal or affine tensor-product calculation is needed.

Write $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})=\{\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\}$. The finite-fibre lemma gives a discrete scheme fibre, and the fibre homeomorphism gives no nontrivial specializations among the $\xi_i$. For any generalization $x$ of $\xi_i$ in $X_0$, $f(x)$ is a generalization of $\eta$. There is no proper generalization of the generic point of a component: the closure of any such generalization is irreducible and contains that maximal component, so equals it, and uniqueness of its generic point forces equality. Hence $f(x)=\eta$ and discreteness forces $x=\xi_i$. Each $\xi_i$ lies in an irreducible component of $X_0$; its generic point exists by sobriety, is a generalization of $\xi_i$, and therefore equals $\xi_i$. Distinct $\xi_i$ belong to distinct components.

Apply the existing theorem exists_isAffineOpen_of_subset_genericPoints to the finite set f⁻¹{η}, which the preceding step shows lies in the generic points of the source. This gives one affine open U containing the entire fibre. This version includes the empty finite set and requires no distinguished point of the fibre.

source.place: Tag 02NW, proof of (1) => (3); Properties Tag 01ZX (lemma-point-and-maximal-points-affine), refinement of 01ZV

proof.text: For the map U → V₀, identify both affine schemes with spectra of their global sections. The affine finite-type criterion makes the global-section ring homomorphism φ finite type. The image p of η is a generic point of a component of Spec R, hence a minimal prime by PrimeSpectrum.mem_genericPoints_iff. Transport finiteness of the set-theoretic fibre through the affine isomorphisms; equality of contracted prime ideals is equivalent to equality of points in Spec R. Apply RingHom.exists_finite_awayMap_of_finite_fiber_minimalPrime to obtain g outside p with finite Localization.awayMap φ g. Mathlib SpecMapRestrictBasicOpenIso identifies restriction to D(g) with Spec of this localized map, and IsFinite.SpecMap_iff proves the restriction finite. Transport back through the affine scheme isomorphisms. The existing restriction/localization isomorphism handles basic-open pullback and localization coordinates directly.

Give the closed complement X₀ ∖ U its reduced closed subscheme structure by IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal, and let j be its inclusion followed by f₀. The inclusion is closed, hence quasi-compact, so j is quasi-compact. If η lies in the closure of range j, exists_specializes_of_mem_closure_range gives t with j(t) specializing to η. Genericity forces j(t)=η, contradicting that U contains the full fibre. Thus W, the complement of that closure, is an open neighbourhood of η with f₀⁻¹(W) contained in U. Intersect W with the finite neighbourhood obtained for U → V₀. Restricting this finite map stays finite. The restriction of U → X₀ over that intersection is an open immersion and is surjective by the preimage containment, hence an isomorphism; cancelling it proves the restriction of f₀ finite. An additional principal-open refinement is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 02NW, proof of (3) => (4), complement removal; its generic-image argument is expanded using the existing closure-specialization theorem (Stacks Tag 02JQ).

proof.text: Let V be the supremum of all open subsets W of Y for which f restricted to W is finite. The preceding local construction shows every component generic point lies in V. Therefore V is dense by dense_of_genericPoints_subset, whose sobriety proof uses that irreducible components cover Y. The opens V.ι⁻¹(W) cover V. By morphismRestrictRestrict and the equality V.ι(image(V.ι⁻¹(W)))=W for W≤V, the restriction of f|V to each is finite. IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_iSup_eq_top then proves f|V finite. If Y is empty the same cover argument is vacuous. There is no intersection across different generic points and no chosen witness is used in a definition.

source.place: Tag 02NW, equivalence (1) and (4) applied at each generic point; union and density argument
